hero.title: Data Center Commissioning.
description: Data center commissioning is a process of isolated or joint tests that ensures all infrastructure operates according to design data and identifies potential failures that could put the mission-critical environment at risk after its start of operation.

This type of service ensures that each component or equipment interconnected to a data center's infrastructure functions properly according to design specifications, delivering reliability and resilience to everyday operations.

types_section.title: Types of data center commissioning.
types_section.description: There are several types of commissioning for data centers which, when performed correctly, improve system performance while reducing costs and energy waste.

items.title: Data center equipment commissioning
items.content: In this type of commissioning, tests are performed to ensure that the installed equipment complies with the manufacturer's specifications and delivers the appropriate operating capacity for the data center.

items.title: Electrical system commissioning
items.content:
Electrical system commissioning is used to test the redundancy of UPS systems and generators. In this process, local utility power is intentionally disconnected to test the generators' capacity to sustain the entire data center operation.

Additionally, infrastructure diagnostics are performed to certify that all equipment and grounding are operating as expected.

items.title: Cooling system commissioning
items.content: This type of commissioning is used to test the effectiveness of the entire data center cooling system. In this phase, the entire set of air conditioning equipment is turned off, and the backup cooling system is automatically activated to meet the environment's demand without affecting data center performance.

items.title: Alarms and sensors commissioning
items.content: In this type of commissioning, tests are performed to validate all internal system alarms and notifications. When a sensor is triggered (e.g., open door, presence of moisture or smoke), the monitoring system must issue alert signals that highlight a threat situation to the data center.

items.title: Fire suppression system commissioning
items.content: In this type of commissioning, all equipment part of the fire suppression system is tested. Should there be any evidence of risk, the fire brigade team will be alerted through the control center.

process_section.title: Commissioning Process
process_section.description: After our specialized team receives the Owner's Project Requirements (OPR), we will initiate the five main stages of the commissioning process.

steps.title: Factory Witness Testing (FWT)
steps.text: This test is performed within the product's factory when mission-critical equipment is purchased from a supplier. The requester will have a copy of the OPR in the purchase specifications, allowing the manufacturer to track and understand expectations before product delivery.

steps.title: Equipment Acceptance Inspection
steps.text: When mission-critical equipment arrives at the data center, it must be verified before being accepted. Equipment can potentially arrive and not match the OPR specifications, making a thorough inspection even more important.

steps.title: Pre-Functional Testing
steps.text:
Tests and further inspections are completed during the installation phase, verifying if all equipment or systems are up to standard and meeting OPR requirements.

The equipment/system is started up to ensure it is working correctly and that there are no issues. However, if there are problems such as duct leaks, fan issues, or pressure gauge problems, they must be resolved and adjusted to the standard, with new tests performed until no failure is detected.

steps.title: Functional Performance Testing
steps.text:
The equipment/system undergoes several complete cycles using all different settings. In this way, the functionalities and performance of all equipment are examined.

It is important that the control loop of each system is examined to ensure the control sequence does what it is intended to do. At this point, equipment is adjusted as necessary and tuned to the OPR.

steps.title: Integrated Systems Testing (IST)
steps.text:
The integrated system test is completed as a final reliability test. To perform this test, the equipment/system will be running and the main power supply is suddenly disconnected to simulate a power outage.

Immediately, the data center's backup power system must take control without issues. Once the test is successfully completed and the OPR is standardized, the data center can begin serving clients with their mission-critical demands.

steps.title: Commissioning Completed
steps.text: After these data center tests, all equipment or systems will have:
checks: High durability;
Optimized maintenance;
Reduction in repairs;
Faster ROI recovery;
Less downtime;
Higher availability rate;
High reliability rate.

hero.title: Data Center Containment Service
description: Consultimer's data center containment service was developed with the goal of reducing PUE (Power Usage Effectiveness) in Data Centers.
Our service is fully focused on enabling temperature control, decreasing energy consumption, and increasing the efficiency of new or existing facilities.

items.title: Cold Aisle Containment (CAC)
paragraphs: The CAC system facilitates the supply of chilled air to equipment with air inlets at a uniform temperature, promoting the physical separation of cold supply air from hot exhaust air by confining the cold aisle.

items.title: Hot Aisle Containment (HAC)
paragraphs: The goal of HAC is to capture hot exhaust air and eliminate it or return it to the cooling units. The rest of the environment becomes a cooled room, providing comfort for Data Center operators.

items.title: Cabinet Vertical Exhaust Duct (VED)
paragraphs: The main objective of VED is to contain exhaust air from the cabinets and prevent the mixing of hot and cold air within production environments. In this system, air is captured through collection systems similar to a 'chimney'.

problems_section.title: Common thermal problems in data centers
problems_section.description: If your Data Center does not have an adequate containment system, your operation is losing money and facing daily risks with:
items: Hot air recirculation from rack exhaust returning to the interior of the equipment;
Leaks due to poor sealing of specific points, such as holes in the raised floor that lead to cold/hot air passing to other aisles;
Insufficient or excessive air capacity for cooling the environment;
Mixing of cold and hot air, leading to a loss of energy efficiency;
Obstruction of air passage, increasing thermal resistance inside the rack;
Incorrect adjustment of CRAC or CRAH system cooling parameters.

benefits_section.title: Benefits of data center containment

hero.title: Allegheny Shredders
description: Consultimer is an authorized Allegheny Shredders distributor in Brazil and offers technical support and special conditions to its customers for the acquisition of the brand's products.

The history of Allegheny Shredders began over 50 years ago when John Wagner started building an industrial shredder to outperform the 7.5 HP paper shredder, which was the most powerful at the time. In 1971, he introduced the first heavy-duty industrial shredder for the paper industry, paving the way for increasingly powerful machines that led to Allegheny's current 300 HP model.
Since those early days, the company has been the icon of the paper shredding and e-scrap industry, widely recognized as the world leader in information destruction.

products.name: Hard Drive Shredder
products.description:
The Hard Drive Shredder is designed to safely and efficiently destroy computer hard drives, optical media, and other electronic devices (phones, cell phones, and thumb drives).

The shredding performed by the equipment provides maximum protection, eliminating any possibility of reconstruction and recovery of sensitive or personal data that must be preserved and secured according to data protection laws (such as LGPD/GDPR). Additionally, the Hard Drive Shredder converts devices that clutter large physical spaces within the company into small fragments.
